# Complete 12-Week Post-MI Conditioning Programme
### Integrated Training, Interval Conditioning, Nutrition, and Clinical Management

---

## Master Reference Document

This is the complete, definitive version of the programme incorporating all phases, progressions, regressions, and clinical decision points. It supersedes all previous partial documents. Read the clinical preamble in full before implementing any component.

---

# CLINICAL PREAMBLE

## Patient Profile and Governing Parameters

**Client:** Male, 58 years old
**Status:** Six months post-myocardial infarction
**Initial clearance:** Phase II cardiac rehabilitation
**Phase III clearance:** Granted at Week 8 transition
**Phase III regression:** Implemented mid-Week 8 following chest tightness during interval training
**Current status:** Phase II parameters reinstated pending cardiologist re-evaluation

## Medication Considerations

Before implementing any component of this programme, confirm the client's full medication list with his cardiologist. The following interactions are clinically relevant and must be understood before training begins.

Beta-blockers blunt the heart rate response to exercise. If the client is taking metoprolol, bisoprolol, carvedilol, or any other beta-blocker, the age-predicted maximum HR of 162 bpm and all derived ceiling values will be artificially suppressed. In this case, RPE becomes the primary intensity guide and HR the secondary guide, rather than the reverse. Confirm with the cardiologist whether the HR ceilings in this programme require adjustment for beta-blocker effect.

Statins interact with grapefruit and grapefruit juice through CYP3A4 inhibition. Grapefruit is eliminated from the nutrition plan entirely.

Warfarin or other anticoagulants interact with vitamin K. If the client is on warfarin, leafy green vegetable intake must remain consistent day to day — do not dramatically increase or decrease consumption, as this destabilises INR. Do not recommend vitamin K supplementation.

ACE inhibitors and potassium-sparing diuretics can cause potassium retention. High-potassium dietary recommendations require confirmation with the prescribing physician before implementation.

## HR Zone Reference Table

| Zone | Name | HR Range | % Max | RPE (Borg 6–20) | Permitted Phase |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Recovery | <100 bpm | <62% | 9–10 | All phases |
| 2 | Aerobic base | 100–112 bpm | 62–69% | 11–12 | Phase I, II, II-return |
| 3 | Moderate | 113–122 bpm | 70–75% | 12–13 | Phase III only |
| 4 | Vigorous | 123–132 bpm | 76–82% | 13–15 | Phase III only |
| 5 | Ceiling approach | 133–136 bpm | 82–85% | 15 | Brief, incidental only |
| — | Hard stop | >136 bpm | >85% | — | Never permitted |

## Parameter Summary by Phase

| Parameter | Phase I (Wks 1–4) | Phase II (Wks 5–8) | Phase III (Wks 8–9 partial) | Phase II Return (Wks 9–12) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HR ceiling | 115 bpm | 115 bpm | 136 bpm | 115 bpm |
| HR working target | 95–108 bpm | 100–112 bpm | 118–132 bpm | 95–110 bpm |
| RPE ceiling | 13/20 | 13/20 | 15/20 | 13/20 |
| Reps in reserve | 4+ | 4+ | 3+ | 4+ |
| Valsalva | None | None | Brief, moderate loads | None |
| Intervals | None | None | MIIT/VIIT | None |
| Sessions/week | 3 | 3–4 | 4–5 | 3 |
| Max session active time | 35 min | 45 min | 55 min | 45 min |

## Universal Monitoring Protocol

The following monitoring requirements apply to every session throughout the entire 12-week programme regardless of phase.

The client wears a chest-strap HR monitor throughout every session. Wrist-based optical sensors are insufficiently accurate for this population and are not acceptable substitutes. HR is checked after every working set during resistance training and every three minutes during cardiovascular work. All readings are recorded in the session log.

Resting HR and blood pressure are checked before every session. If resting systolic BP exceeds 160 mmHg or diastolic exceeds 100 mmHg, the session does not proceed. The client rests, the reading is recorded, and the cardiologist is contacted if elevated readings persist across two consecutive days.

Symptom screening is conducted verbally before every session. Ask the client directly about chest discomfort, tightness, pressure, or pain since the last session; unusual breathlessness at rest or with light activity; palpitations or irregular heartbeat sensations; dizziness or lightheadedness; and unusual fatigue disproportionate to recent activity. Any positive response means no training that day. If symptoms are ongoing or worsening, contact the cardiologist.

## Emergency Action Protocol

Stop immediately and call emergency services if the client experiences chest pain or pressure of any kind during exercise, jaw or left arm pain or discomfort, severe breathlessness beyond expected exertion, dizziness or pre-syncope, syncope, palpitations or irregular heartbeat, or unusual pallor and sweating. Do not wait to see if symptoms resolve. Do not drive the client to hospital. Call emergency services, keep the client still and seated or lying down depending on symptoms, retrieve the AED, and begin CPR if the client loses consciousness and is not breathing normally. Your CPR certification must be current. The AED location must be known before every session begins.

## Breathing Protocol

Because Valsalva is prohibited in Phases I, II, and the Phase II return period, every resistance exercise uses continuous breathing throughout. Exhale on the concentric phase (the effort — the press, the pull, the stand, the drive). Inhale on the eccentric phase (the return — the lower, the release, the sit). Cue this verbally on every set for the first four weeks and whenever lapses are observed thereafter. In Phase III only, a brief moderate intra-abdominal brace of one to two seconds is permitted at the sticking point of moderate-load compound lifts, followed immediately by a controlled exhale. This is withdrawn entirely during the Phase II return period.

## Baseline Assessments (Week 0)

Complete the following before Week 1 begins. Results establish the baseline against which progress is measured at Weeks 4, 8, and 12.

Six-Minute Walk Test: record total distance covered and HR response throughout. Note the HR at the end of each minute and the peak HR achieved.

Thirty-second chair stand test: count the number of times the client can stand from a standard chair and return to seated in 30 seconds without using his arms.

Grip strength: measure with a hand dynamometer, three trials each hand, record the best result for each.

Resting HR and blood pressure: measure after five minutes of seated rest.

Movement screen: observe the squat pattern, hip hinge pattern, overhead reach, and single-leg balance. Note any limitations, asymmetries, or compensations.

---

# NUTRITION PLAN — CARDIAC HEALTH FOCUS

## Governing Principles

The nutrition plan operates throughout all 12 weeks and is adjusted by phase to reflect changing training demands. It is designed to complement medical dietary advice, not replace it. A referral to a registered dietitian with cardiovascular specialism is strongly recommended alongside this plan.

## Caloric Framework

Using the Mifflin-St Jeor equation for a 58-year-old male at approximately 82 kg and 175 cm:

Resting Metabolic Rate: (10 × 82) + (6.25 × 175) − (5 × 58) + 5 = approximately 1,629 kcal per day.

Activity multiplier of 1.4 in Phases I and II gives approximately 2,280 kcal per day. Activity multiplier of 1.55 in Phase III gives approximately 2,525 kcal per day. During the Phase II return period, return to the 1.4 multiplier — approximately 2,280 kcal per day. Adjust all values for the client's actual body weight.

If weight loss is a secondary goal confirmed by the cardiologist, apply a modest deficit of 200–300 kcal per day through food quality and composition rather than severe restriction.

## Macronutrient Targets

**Protein:** 1.4–1.6 g per kilogram of body weight per day. For an 82 kg client, this means 115–131 g of protein daily. Distribute across at least four eating occasions with 25–35 g per meal. Older adults experience anabolic resistance and require more dietary protein per kilogram than younger adults to achieve equivalent muscle protein synthesis.

Preferred sources: oily fish (salmon, mackerel, sardines, trout), skinless poultry, eggs, legumes (lentils, chickpeas, black beans, kidney beans), low-fat Greek yoghurt, cottage cheese, tofu, tempeh, edamame.

Sources to minimise: processed red meat (bacon, sausages, salami, deli meats) is largely eliminated. Unprocessed red meat is limited to 350–500 g cooked weight per week maximum.

**Carbohydrates:** 45–55% of total calories from carbohydrate, emphasising low-glycaemic, high-fibre sources. For a 2,200 kcal diet, approximately 248–303 g per day.

Preferred sources: rolled oats (75 g dry daily provides 3 g of beta-glucan for LDL reduction), sweet potato, new potatoes with skin, brown rice, quinoa, barley, wholegrain bread, berries, all vegetables.

Sources to minimise: white bread, white rice, refined pasta in large quantities, sugary drinks including fruit juice, pastries, biscuits, confectionery, ultra-processed foods.

Peri-workout strategy: a small carbohydrate and protein snack 60–90 minutes before training on training days. A banana with nut butter, or a small bowl of porridge. Post-session, a carbohydrate and protein combination within 30–60 minutes — Greek yoghurt with berries, or a wholegrain wrap with chicken and salad.

**Fats:** 30–35% of total calories from fat, strongly emphasising unsaturated fats. For a 2,200 kcal diet, approximately 73–86 g per day.

Preferred sources: extra-virgin olive oil as the primary cooking and dressing fat (2–4 tablespoons daily), oily fish three to four times per week for EPA and DHA omega-3 fatty acids, a 30 g handful of mixed nuts daily (walnuts, almonds, pistachios), avocado, ground flaxseed, chia seeds, hemp seeds.

Saturated fat: below 7% of total calories, approximately 17 g per day. Reduce fatty red meat, butter, cream, full-fat cheese, coconut oil, palm oil.

Trans fats: eliminated entirely. Avoid any product listing partially hydrogenated oil in the ingredients.

## The Five Cardiac Nutrition Pillars

**Pillar 1 — Mediterranean pattern as the overarching framework.** Abundant vegetables and fruit, legumes as a protein staple, whole grains, olive oil as the primary fat, regular oily fish, moderate poultry and eggs, limited red meat, minimal processed foods. Alcohol: discuss with the cardiologist. Current guidance does not recommend alcohol for cardiovascular benefit. Strict moderation or abstinence is the conservative position.

**Pillar 2 — Sodium management.** Target no more than 2,000 mg of sodium per day. Cook from scratch where possible. Use herbs, spices, lemon juice, and vinegar instead of salt. Choose tinned fish and vegetables in no-added-salt varieties. Read labels — above 0.6 g of salt per 100 g is considered high.

**Pillar 3 — Dietary fibre.** Target 30–35 g per day. Soluble fibre from oats, barley, legumes, apples, and psyllium husk binds bile acids and lowers LDL. Increase fibre gradually over two to three weeks if the client is currently eating a low-fibre diet. Increase water intake alongside fibre increases.

**Pillar 4 — Plant sterols and stanols.** 2 g per day from fortified foods (Flora ProActiv, Benecol, fortified yoghurt drinks) can reduce LDL by 10–15% when consumed consistently with meals. Discuss with the cardiologist before implementing.

**Pillar 5 — Hydration.** 2.0–2.5 litres of fluid per day, increasing to 2.5–3.0 litres on training days. Water is the primary fluid. Unsweetened herbal teas and green tea are appropriate alternatives. Caffeine up to 300–400 mg per day is generally safe but confirm with the cardiologist.

## Phase-Specific Nutrition Adjustments

**Phases I and II (Weeks 1–8):** Working caloric target 2,100–2,300 kcal per day. Focus on eliminating processed meats, sugary drinks, and trans fats in Week 1. Build the breakfast habit around porridge with berries, ground flaxseed, and walnuts. Introduce oily fish three times per week from Week 1. Introduce legumes as a daily staple from Week 5. Optimise post-session recovery nutrition from Week 5 — protein and carbohydrate within 30 minutes of resistance sessions.

**Phase III (Weeks 8–9 partial):** Increase daily caloric intake by 150–200 kcal on training days to support higher training volume. Add one extra serving of complex carbohydrate pre- or post-training. Maintain protein at 1.6 g per kilogram. Ensure pre-training meal of carbohydrate and protein 90–120 minutes before training. Discuss creatine monohydrate (3–5 g per day) with the cardiologist — growing evidence base for cardiovascular safety and potential benefit for increased strength training demands.

**Phase II Return (Weeks 9–12):** Return to Phase I and II caloric targets — 2,100–2,300 kcal per day. Maintain all dietary quality standards. Emphasise anti-inflammatory foods during this period: increase omega-3 rich fish, berries, leafy greens, turmeric, and ginger. Reduce any dietary stressors — excessive caffeine, alcohol if present, high-sodium convenience foods — that may contribute to cardiovascular reactivity. Ensure the client is eating adequately before sessions — hypoglycaemia during exercise is a cardiovascular stressor that must be avoided.

---

---

# PHASE 1 — FOUNDATION
## Weeks 1–4

**Phase goals:** Establish safe HR response to exercise. Build movement competency. Develop the continuous breathing habit as automatic. Create a positive psychological relationship with the gym environment post-cardiac event. Establish baseline fitness metrics.

**Resistance parameters:** 2–3 sets | 12–15 reps | RPE 10–12 | Minimum 4 reps in reserve | Rest 90–120 seconds between sets | Tempo: 2 seconds eccentric, 1 second pause, 1–2 seconds concentric.

**Cardiovascular parameters:** Continuous steady-state only. HR target 95–108 bpm. RPE 10–11. Recumbent bike is the primary modality.

**Sessions per week:** Three. Minimum one full rest day between each session.

---

## WEEK 1

### Session 1 — Lower Body and Core Focus

**Warm-up (10 minutes)**

Five minutes on the recumbent bike at minimal resistance. HR should reach 85–95 bpm. Follow with five minutes of mobility: 10 seated thoracic rotations each side (sit tall, arms crossed over chest, rotate slowly), 10 ankle circles each direction, 10 glute bridges on the floor (feet flat, drive hips to ceiling, squeeze glutes at the top, lower with control — exhale on the drive up), 10 hip circles each direction.

Check HR before proceeding to working sets. It should be below 95 bpm.

**Working sets**

*Seated leg press — 2 sets × 15 reps.*
Feet hip-width apart on the platform, toes slightly out. Press through the whole foot — do not rise onto the toes. Do not lock the knees at the top. Lower under control for 2 seconds. Exhale on the press, inhale on the lower. Load: start conservatively — the client should feel the effort but be nowhere near failure. Check HR after each set. Rest 2 minutes.

*Glute bridge (floor, bilateral) — 2 sets × 15 reps.*
Lie on the floor, knees bent, feet flat. Drive the hips to the ceiling by squeezing the glutes. Hold 1 second at the top. Lower with control. Exhale on the drive up. Bodyweight only. Rest 60 seconds.

*Goblet squat to high box — 2 sets × 12 reps.*
Box height at chair level. Light dumbbell (4–6 kg) or bodyweight. Feet hip-width apart, toes out 15–30 degrees. Sit back to the box, stand tall. Exhale on the stand. Rest 90 seconds.

*Seated leg curl — 2 sets × 15 reps.*
Light load. Exhale on the curl, inhale on the return. Rest 90 seconds.

*Seated calf raise — 2 sets × 20 reps.*
Bodyweight or light plate on thighs. Full range of motion — lower the heel below the platform level, rise fully onto the ball of the foot. Rest 60 seconds.

*Dead bug — 2 sets × 8 reps each side.*
Lie on the back, knees bent to 90 degrees, arms pointing to the ceiling. Slowly lower one arm overhead while extending the opposite leg, keeping the lower back pressed gently into the floor. Breathe continuously — exhale as the limbs extend. If the client holds their breath at any point, stop the set. Rest 60 seconds.

**Cool-down (10 minutes)**

Five minutes slow treadmill walk at 2.5 km/h, flat. Five minutes seated stretching: standing hip flexor lunge (30 seconds each side), supine hamstring stretch (30 seconds each side), seated calf stretch (30 seconds each side). Final HR check — below 90 bpm before leaving.

---

### Session 2 — Cardiovascular Conditioning

**Warm-up:** Five minutes recumbent bike at minimal resistance.

**Main work:** 20 minutes on the recumbent bike. HR target 95–108 bpm. RPE 10–11. The client should be able to speak in full sentences throughout. Check HR every 3 minutes and record it. If HR climbs above 108 bpm, reduce resistance immediately.

**Why the recumbent bike in Week 1:** The recumbent position reduces cardiac preload compared to upright exercise and eliminates balance demands, making it the safest cardiovascular starting point for this population.

**Cool-down:** Five minutes at minimal resistance. Five minutes seated rest with HR monitoring.

---

### Session 3 — Upper Body and Core Focus

**Warm-up (10 minutes)**

Five minutes recumbent bike. Then: 10 arm circles each direction, 10 wall slides (arms slide up a wall, elbows bent to 90 degrees, press the arms overhead while keeping the back of the hands and elbows in contact with the wall), 15 band pull-aparts (light resistance band held in both hands at shoulder height, pull the band apart by squeezing the shoulder blades together).

**Working sets**

*Seated cable row (close grip, neutral handles) — 2 sets × 15 reps.*
Sit tall. Initiate the movement by retracting the shoulder blades before bending the elbows. Pull the handles to the lower sternum. Return with control. Exhale on the pull, inhale on the return. Light load. Rest 2 minutes.

*Chest press machine — 2 sets × 15 reps.*
Light load. Exhale on the press. Rest 90 seconds.

*Lat pulldown (wide grip, to chin level) — 2 sets × 15 reps.*
Do not pull behind the neck. Lean back very slightly — approximately 10–15 degrees — and pull the bar to the upper chest. Exhale on the pull-down. Light load. Rest 90 seconds.

*Dumbbell shoulder press (seated) — 2 sets × 12 reps.*
Very light load (3–5 kg). Exhale on the press. Rest 90 seconds.

*Band pull-apart — 2 sets × 15 reps.*
Light band. Arms straight at shoulder height, pull the band apart until the arms are in a T position, squeezing the shoulder blades together. Rest 60 seconds.

*Wall push-up or incline push-up — 2 sets × 10 reps.*
Begin with wall push-ups if the client cannot perform a knee push-up with continuous breathing and controlled tempo. Exhale on the push away from the wall. Rest 90 seconds.

*Dead bug — 2 sets × 8 reps each side.*
As per Session 1. Rest 60 seconds.

**Cool-down (10 minutes)**

Five minutes slow treadmill walk. Five minutes stretching: chest doorway stretch (30 seconds), lat stretch with arm overhead against wall (30 seconds each side), neck side flexion (20 seconds each side — gentle, no overpressure).
